first.rationale: Prioritize verification of the two most consequential competing beliefs: whether onboarding simplification still reliably improves adoption and whether promotional pricing produces sustainable qualified revenue under price competition. Current declines in both onboarding completion and activation make a simplified onboarding experiment the most direct route to restoring durable product adoption, while pricing may trade acquisition volume for lower-quality or less durable revenue.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The verified onboarding result directly addresses both current declines: completion increased 13%, time-to-value fell 2.1 days, and 30-day retention increased 3%. By contrast, verified promotional pricing generated short-term qualified revenue but materially reduced retention and failed the sustainable-growth criterion. Measure activation, qualified conversion, and retention by segment to confirm the prior effect persists under current conditions.
